clock_scopes.node_local: Both events observed by one process on one host clock, or a pure count.
clock_scopes.same_clock_domain: Events may be on different hosts; manifest clocks.clock_domain must be single_clock or synchronized.

metrics.title: Sensor-to-policy request delay
metrics.start_event: source timestamp of an observation message (stamped where the sensor/simulator produces it)
metrics.end_event: the policy client sends the inference request that uses that observation
metrics.clock_requirement: Sensor stamp and request send may be taken on different hosts: needs clock_domain single_clock or synchronized (with the manifest's estimated_max_offset). unsynchronized => not_computable.
metrics.censoring_rule: Not censorable. Observations that never produce a request are not samples; if there are no samples the status is not_computable (no_samples).
metrics.failed_run_rule: A failed/aborted run keeps whatever post-warmup samples exist; with none it is not_computable, never 0.
metrics.applicable_when: Always, when a policy client consumes sensor observations.
does_not_show: Network or serving time (only the client-side wait before the request is sent).
Anything about tails: one median per run hides p95/p99 and bursts.
That the observation was fresh when acted on (see action_age_ms).

metrics.title: Request-serve-response delay
metrics.start_event: the policy client sends an inference request
metrics.end_event: the same client receives the matching response
metrics.clock_requirement: Both timestamps are taken by the client process, so a single clock on that host is enough. Do not substitute server-side timestamps.
metrics.censoring_rule: Requests with no response before the run ends are counted in failure_count, not averaged in; they are not samples.
metrics.failed_run_rule: Same as above: partial runs keep their samples; none => not_computable.
metrics.applicable_when: Always, when a remote or local inference request/response exists.
does_not_show: How the time splits between network, queueing and model compute (needs server-side tracing).
Quality of the returned action.
Behaviour of the failed requests that never got a response (they are excluded from the median and counted elsewhere).

metrics.title: Validator delay
metrics.start_event: the validator receives a candidate action
metrics.end_event: the validator emits its verdict (accept or typed reject)
metrics.clock_requirement: Both events are observed in the validator process: single clock on its host.
metrics.censoring_rule: Candidates still unprocessed at run end are not samples; they are not silently dropped from failure accounting.
metrics.failed_run_rule: Partial runs keep their samples; none => not_computable.
metrics.applicable_when: Always, when an action validator sits between policy and sink.
does_not_show: That the validator is correct or safe (it measures time, not verdict quality).
Anything about actuation: this contract is non-actuating.

metrics.title: Action age at release
metrics.start_event: source timestamp of the observation the action was computed from
metrics.end_event: the validator releases the action to the (non-actuating, simulated or logged) sink
metrics.clock_requirement: Start and end are usually on different hosts: needs clock_domain single_clock or synchronized. unsynchronized => not_computable; a skewed wall clock can make ages negative, which is a data error, not a result.
metrics.censoring_rule: Actions never released (rejected or still buffered at run end) are not samples; rejections are visible via failure_count and deadline_miss_fraction denominators.
metrics.failed_run_rule: Partial runs keep their samples; none => not_computable.
metrics.applicable_when: Always, when actions are released to a sink.
does_not_show: Control quality, task success or safety.
Tail behaviour (median per run only).
Real actuator or motor latency: the sink is non-actuating.

metrics.title: Action-buffer starvation fraction
metrics.per_run_reduction: starved_ticks / control_ticks over the post-warmup window (both integers are stored)
metrics.end_event: the action buffer was empty at that tick (counts as starved)
metrics.clock_requirement: A count of ticks on one node; no cross-host comparison. The tick source must be the control-rate timer declared in the manifest.
metrics.censoring_rule: Ticks that did not happen because the run stopped are not counted; control_ticks = 0 gives not_computable (no_samples), never 0/0.
metrics.failed_run_rule: Counted over the ticks that occurred before the failure; the run is flagged by status/failure_count, not hidden.
metrics.applicable_when: Always, when the policy loop uses an action buffer or chunking.
does_not_show: Why the buffer was empty (slow model, network loss, validator rejects).
Whether starved ticks held the previous action or did nothing (a policy choice outside this metric).

metrics.title: Deadline-miss fraction
metrics.per_run_reduction: missed_actions / released_actions over the post-warmup window (both integers are stored)
metrics.start_event: an action is released to the sink
metrics.end_event: its age exceeds timing.action_age_deadline from the manifest (strictly greater = miss; age equal to the deadline is a hit)
metrics.clock_requirement: Uses action age, so the same clock requirement as action_age_ms. unsynchronized => not_computable.
metrics.censoring_rule: Only released actions are in the denominator; actions never released are not counted as misses here (see failure_count). released_actions = 0 gives not_computable.
metrics.failed_run_rule: Counted over the actions released before the failure.
metrics.applicable_when: Always, when action_age_deadline is declared (it is required in the manifest).
does_not_show: A hard-real-time guarantee: this is a soft statistic over a finite run.
Whether a late action was harmful.

metrics.title: Largest message gap
metrics.per_run_reduction: maximum gap in the post-warmup window (a maximum, not a median)
metrics.start_event: reception of one observation message at the policy client
metrics.end_event: reception of the next message on the same topic at the same client
metrics.clock_requirement: Both receptions are timestamped by the same client process: single clock on that host.
metrics.censoring_rule: A gap still open when the run ends is not counted as a gap (it is a lower bound on a longer outage that this metric does not report).
metrics.failed_run_rule: Counted over messages received before the failure; fewer than 2 messages => not_computable (no_samples).
metrics.applicable_when: Always, when the policy client subscribes to an observation topic.
does_not_show: Where the loss happened (publisher, DDS, CNI, subscriber).
How many gaps occurred (see message_gap_count).

metrics.title: Message-gap count
metrics.per_run_reduction: number of gaps larger than 2 x the nominal period (1 / timing.control_rate) in the post-warmup window
metrics.start_event: reception of one observation message at the policy client
metrics.end_event: the next reception is later than 2 x nominal period (strictly greater)
metrics.clock_requirement: Receiver-local timestamps only: single clock on the client host.
metrics.censoring_rule: As for message_gap_max_ms: an open gap at run end is not counted.
metrics.failed_run_rule: Counted over messages received before the failure.
metrics.applicable_when: Always, when the policy client subscribes to an observation topic.
does_not_show: Gap length (see message_gap_max_ms) or cause.
That the threshold (2 x nominal) is the right one for a given robot task.

metrics.title: Recovery time after an injected fault
metrics.per_run_reduction: one value per run: the first recovery after the injected fault
metrics.start_event: the injected fault ends (manifest fault_injection.duration elapsed)
metrics.end_event: the validator releases its first valid action again
metrics.clock_requirement: The fault controller and the validator may run on different hosts: needs single_clock or synchronized. unsynchronized => not_computable.
metrics.censoring_rule: RIGHT-CENSORED when the run ends or times out before recovery: status censored, value null, and censored_lower_bound = observed time without recovery. A censored run is never averaged in as if it recovered at the timeout, and a summary that contains censored runs withholds any interval.
metrics.failed_run_rule: A failed run that never recovered is censored (not dropped and not set to the timeout).
metrics.applicable_when: Only when manifest fault_injection.applied is true; otherwise not_applicable.
does_not_show: That the system is resilient in general (one fault type, one run).
Recovery of the task itself, only of valid-action release.

metrics.title: Per-run failure count
metrics.per_run_reduction: number of failure events in the run; must equal manifest outcome.failure_count
metrics.start_event: the run starts (failures during warmup are counted too)
metrics.censoring_rule: Failed, timed-out and aborted runs are INCLUDED with their counts (never dropped); a timed-out or aborted run has failure_count >= 1.
metrics.failed_run_rule: Always counted. The number of attempted runs is the denominator of every failure rate; do not report rates over successful runs only.
does_not_show: The kind or severity of each failure (record kinds in the raw log).
A failure rate by itself: it needs the number of independent runs.

metrics.title: Task success (only when applicable)
metrics.per_run_reduction: true/false for the run's task outcome under a pre-declared success criterion
metrics.end_event: the pre-declared success criterion is evaluated
metrics.censoring_rule: A run that timed out before the criterion could be evaluated is a failure (false) only if the criterion declares it so; otherwise not_computable. Never silently dropped.
metrics.failed_run_rule: Counted in the denominator whenever the metric is applicable.
metrics.applicable_when: Only when manifest outcome.task_success.applicable is true. A transport-level experiment has no task, and reports not_applicable instead of an invented success.
does_not_show: Physical task success: this repository records simulation or synthetic outcomes only.
Generalisation beyond the declared task, seeds and simulator.
